note: Which slot a GM-side entry or `slot` frame is about: the table, or ONE participant by id. It is deliberately not a RevealAudience — under owner decision O-3 an audience may name several participants, because one Confirm fills one slot per recipient with copies of one disclosure, while a slot is one region of one screen and names one participant. It travels on the GM channel and in GmSnapshot only: a table client is told `table` or `mine` and never an id (SEC-15, threat model 8.2). An alias is a display name and never leaves the GM's channel (AUD-11).

valid.name: a participant whose id is the word table

invalid.name: a recipient list where a slot belongs
invalid.why: owner decision O-3: an audience may name several participants, but a slot is one region of one screen — a list here would be a slot with two screens

invalid.name: a participant slot with no id
invalid.why: ED-10: a slot is named by an identity; there is nothing to address without one

invalid.name: an alias beside the id
invalid.why: AUD-11: an alias is a display name and never leaves the GM's channel, so it is refused even where the id beside it is correct

invalid.name: the table slot carrying a participant id
invalid.why: the table is not a participant; one shape per slot, and no half-named region

invalid.name: the table client's own slot name
invalid.why: SEC-15: `mine` is how a TABLE client is told which region a projection belongs in, because that side is id-free; the GM's picture names the participant, so the two vocabularies never meet

invalid.name: a bare string
invalid.why: a slot reference is a discriminated object, so a second kind cannot be added by string

invalid.name: a participant id outside the id alphabet
